propositions.title: Clean Drinking Water & Climate Resilience Bond
propositions.yesVoteMeaning: Authorizes $10 billion in general obligation bonds to fund water purification, flood protection, wildfire prevention, and reservoir modernization.
propositions.noVoteMeaning: The state would not issue new bonds for water and climate resilience projects, and existing revenue would be relied upon.
propositions.fiscalSummary: Estimated state cost of approximately $400 million annually over 30 years to repay bond principal and interest from the general fund.
propositions.proponents: California Firefighters, League of California Cities, Conservation organizations
propositions.opponents: Taxpayers Coalition (arguing against increased state debt and interest payments)

propositions.title: Public School Facility Repair & STEM Modernization Bond
propositions.yesVoteMeaning: Authorizes $8.5 billion to renovate aging K-12 public schools, replace lead pipes, and build modern science and technology laboratories.
propositions.noVoteMeaning: Local school districts would have to rely solely on local parcel taxes and existing budgets for facility repairs.
propositions.fiscalSummary: Annual debt service of roughly $350 million paid over 30 years from the state General Fund.
propositions.proponents: California Teachers Association, State PTA, School Board Association

propositions.title: Affordable Housing Construction & Tenant Protection Act
propositions.yesVoteMeaning: Allows local communities to streamline permits for multi-family affordable housing and establishes minimum tenant notification standards.
propositions.noVoteMeaning: Maintains current local zoning discretion and existing statutory eviction procedures.
propositions.fiscalSummary: Minor direct state cost, potential long-term increase in local property tax revenue from new housing developments.
propositions.proponents: Habitat for Humanity, California Nurses Association, Housing advocacy groups
propositions.opponents: California Apartment Association, Commercial real estate groups

propositions.title: Texas Electrical Grid Resiliency & Emergency Generation Fund
propositions.yesVoteMeaning: Amends the Texas Constitution to allocate $5 billion from the state budget surplus into a low-interest loan fund for dispatchable thermal energy and grid winterization.
propositions.noVoteMeaning: No dedicated constitutional reserve fund would be created; grid investments would remain market-driven.
propositions.fiscalSummary: One-time transfer of $5 billion from surplus revenues. No new taxes required.
propositions.proponents: Texas Chamber of Commerce, Manufacturing Association, Electric Reliability Council
propositions.opponents: Consumer advocacy groups urging greater renewable energy access and lower residential rate impacts

propositions.title: Prohibition on Wealth Taxes and Statewide Property Levies
propositions.yesVoteMeaning: Constitutional amendment prohibiting the state legislature from imposing any tax based on the net worth or wealth of an individual or business.
propositions.noVoteMeaning: The Texas Legislature retains its current constitutional taxing authority without an explicit ban on net-worth taxes.
propositions.fiscalSummary: No current fiscal impact since Texas does not impose a wealth tax.
propositions.proponents: Texas Taxpayers and Research Association, Governor Abbott
propositions.opponents: Texas Progressive Caucus, Public Policy Center

propositions.title: Clean Water, Clean Air and Green Jobs Implementation Amendment
propositions.yesVoteMeaning: Adds explicit constitutional protections guaranteeing every New Yorker clean water, clean air, and a healthful environment with legal standing to enforce.
propositions.noVoteMeaning: Existing statutory environmental protections remain in place without explicit constitutional entitlement.
propositions.fiscalSummary: Potential administrative and judicial costs depending on volume of enforcement petitions.
propositions.proponents: Environmental Advocates NY, Sierra Club Atlantic Chapter

propositions.title: Partisan School Board Elections Requirement
propositions.yesVoteMeaning: Requires candidates for district school boards to run with political party affiliations on the ballot, ending nonpartisan school board elections.
propositions.noVoteMeaning: School board candidates continue to appear on the ballot without party labels.
propositions.fiscalSummary: No significant fiscal impact on state or local government.
propositions.opponents: League of Women Voters of Florida, Florida PTA

propositions.title: Bipartisan Congressional Term Limits Advisory Measure
propositions.yesVoteMeaning: Advises state legislatures and Congress to propose a constitutional amendment limiting U.S. Senators to two 6-year terms and House Members to six 2-year terms.
propositions.noVoteMeaning: Maintains current system without term limits on federal legislators.
propositions.fiscalSummary: Non-binding national advisory referendum with no direct fiscal impact.
